minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted a special permit for a belt fabrication business at 100 Pleasant Street, and one for a four-dog daycare.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Zoning Board of Appeals, sitting with four members, heard two special permit applications. It granted a permit to extend a non-conforming use at 100 Pleasant Street for belt distribution and fabrication, with hours limited to 7 to 6 Monday through Friday. It then granted a continued application for a doggy daycare at 1432 Lancaster Avenue, limited to four dogs at a time.

public_comment.topic: A neighbor across the street had no issue with the business but asked to limit evening hours and early or late deliveries.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit for 100 Pleasant Street with hours of operation 7 to 6, Monday through Friday.
Grant the special permit for the doggy daycare for up to four dogs at a time, 6:30 to 6:30, with the submitted details as conditions.

decisions.decision: The chair offered applicants the choice to proceed with four members or wait for a full board; both hearings went ahead with four members, requiring all four in the affirmative.
The animal control officer said she can issue a four-dog kennel license once the applicant has called her to inspect.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit to extend a non-conforming use at 100 Pleasant Street for belt distribution and fabrication, 4-0, with hours of 7 to 6, Monday through Friday.
The board then granted a special permit for a doggy daycare at 1432 Lancaster Avenue, limited to four dogs at a time, with the submitted details as conditions.
Both hearings went ahead with four members after the chair offered applicants the choice to wait for a full board; all four had to vote yes.
A neighbor across from 100 Pleasant Street raised no objection but asked for limits on evening hours and early or late deliveries.
The animal control officer said she can issue a four-dog kennel license once the applicant has called her to inspect.

why_it_matters: These permits set what can operate at two local addresses, including hours and, for the daycare, the number of dogs, which affects neighbors on Pleasant Street and Lancaster Avenue.
watch_next: The daycare still needs a four-dog kennel license from animal control, which the officer said she can issue once the applicant calls her to inspect.
